t: The Chimú built Chan Chan around 850 CE as the capital of Chimor, a conquest state on the Peruvian coast, and it held an estimated 40,000 to 60,000 people.
The city rested on canals that carried water from the Moche river, and its rulers lived in ten walled ciudadelas while artisans worked in small rooms that doubled as workshops.
The Incas conquered the Chimú around 1470 and dispersed them, the Spaniards looted the city after Pizarro founded Trujillo in 1535, and excavations began in 1969.
dyk: The Chimú held that the sun created three eggs: gold for the ruler and the elite, silver for the rulers' spouses, and copper for everyone else.
ev: Chan Chan is the capital of the Chimor kingdom from about this year
A catastrophic flood destroys many of the canals to the north
The Incas defeat the Chimú and incorporate Chimor into their empire
Francisco Pizarro founds the Spanish city of Trujillo nearby
Michael Moseley and Carol J. Mackey begin excavations
UNESCO designates Chan Chan a World Heritage Site and lists it as in danger

f.founded: Believed to have been constructed around 850 CE by the Chimú; the city was the capital of Chimor from 900 to 1470.
f.where: At the mouth of the Moche Valley in the coastal desert of northern Peru, in the department of La Libertad, five kilometres west of Trujillo and close to the Pacific Ocean.
f.known: Capital of the Chimor kingdom; ten walled ciudadelas of adobe; carved reliefs of fish, birds and nets; canal irrigation from the Moche river; Chimú pottery and textiles; conquest by the Incas around 1470; looting by the Spaniards
f.today: Chan Chan is an archaeological site and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1986, and has been called the largest adobe city in the Americas.
